thought.text: npm install is complete. Now let me start the backend build and monitor the Keycloak repro:

reasoning_content:
npm install completed. node_modules is already placed. Next, while keycloak's reproduction environment is starting up (which takes about 60–90 seconds), start the backend build. The backend build target builds the webpack bundle. Let's run `npx nx run startuphafen-backend:build:development`. This might take a while.

Actually, wait — `serve` builds in watch mode. To get a persistent process with less overhead, I could just run the pre-built backend directly: `node dist/apps/startuphafen-backend/main.js`. But main.ts uses `__dirname` for assets (getAssetPath) — the webpack build copies assets to dist/apps/startuphafen-backend/assets. Good — that's why assets is included in the build options.

Let me start the backend build in the background, and in the meantime monitor the keycloak reproduction.

action.command:
cd /workspace && nohup npx nx run startuphafen-backend:build:development > /tmp/backend_build.log 2>&1 &
echo "backend build started: $!"
